lines.text: Two hundred people, two hundred different rhythms.
It locks. Everybody together, and nobody said a word.
Physicists recorded this in concert halls, and put numbers on it.
You are not keeping your own time. You are listening.
Every clap lands a little early, or a little late, pulled toward the room.
Two hundred people all nudging each other has only one place to end up.
But watch what the room has to give up to get there.
Clapping fast, everyone's natural rate is too spread out. The pull is not strong enough.
So the room halves its speed. Now the spread is half as wide, and it fits.
Then it gets loud, and it drifts, and the room comes apart again.
There is no conductor in an audience. There never was.
